title: Run the logquery capstone: build on logfmt, kill 18/20 mutants, aggregate, prove the CLI three ways
goal: The band capstone chains four stages over a log-analysis stack built on the shipped sealed logfmt parser. Stage 1 implements loading and typed filtering on top of the sealed parser; stage 2 hardens that dependency by killing at least 18 of 20 sealed logfmt mutants (quote escapes, flag keys, duplicate-key and empty-value semantics hide the stubborn survivors); stage 3 adds aggregations with exact rounding and ordering contracts; stage 4 ships a CLI proven three independent ways - byte-exact sealed goldens, a grader-executed determinism double-run, and a probe log generated fresh at grading time and checked against the grader's internal reference, so memorizing goldens cannot pass. A frozen plan, four hash-chained markers, an 8-entry run journal, and an honest cost record are graded with final state as one campaign_score.
resources: pypi pytest==8.3.4 (installed by the sealed grader inside the container)
assets/gc-419/SPEC.md (module, mutation, and CLI contracts + artifact contract)
assets/gc-419/grade.py + assets/gc-419/config.json (sealed campaign grader with probe generator)
process_expectations: A frozen four-stage plan predates code and survives the campaign unmodified, proven by the sha256 chain plan -> stage1 -> ... -> stage4.
Kill-test work is behavioral and identity-driven: no source introspection (grader-enforced), and runs.log stage-2 entries show the kill count climbing across at least two grading attempts.
runs.log carries at least 8 honest entries spanning all four stages, including RED runs with their real failed counts.
The CLI is proven against unseen data: the grader-generated probe log must reproduce its reference count-by output exactly, on top of byte-exact goldens and an identical double-run.
cost.json reports honest llm_usd and grader_runs for the whole campaign; earlier suites are re-run at the end to catch late regressions.

assets_visibility.note: sealed files live in the maintainers' private sealed pack; public repo keeps <name>.sha256 commitments. Restore with tools/restore_sealed.py before grading these cards.
